**Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality**

**Location:** Lakewood, Ohio  
**Company:** Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company  
**Employment Type:** Full Time  
**Reports To:** President

**About Ferry Cap**

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is a long-established American manufacturer of engineered fasteners and specialty metal components serving demanding industrial and power generation applications. As we invest in our people, equipment, and operating systems, we are seeking a senior quality leader who can help strengthen our processes and build a companywide culture of quality.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will lead Ferry Cap’s quality organization and serve as a key member of the company’s leadership team.

This is a hands on leadership position for someone with strong experience in metallurgy, metal transformation, manufacturing processes, and heat treatment. The successful candidate will work closely with operations, engineering, maintenance, supply chain, and customers to improve process control, solve technical problems, and ensure consistent product quality.

The right leader will view quality as an operating partnership, not simply an inspection function. This individual must be comfortable working on the production floor, engaging directly with employees, and helping build quality into every stage of the manufacturing process.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all quality assurance, quality control, laboratory, inspection, and quality systems activities.
* Partner directly with operations to establish a culture in which safety, delivery, quality, and cost are shared responsibilities.
* Provide technical leadership related to metallurgy, raw materials, metal forming, metal transformation, machining, threading, and heat treatment.
* Oversee metallurgical testing and analysis, including hardness, microstructure, case depth, decarburization, mechanical properties, material certification, and failure analysis.
* Evaluate and improve heat treatment processes, including furnace controls, quenching, tempering, process consistency, and product conformance.
* Strengthen incoming, in process, and final inspection systems to ensure product requirements are consistently achieved.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action activities involving internal defects, customer complaints, supplier issues, and process failures.
* Use structured problem solving methods such as 8D, 5 Why, fishbone analysis, PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and MSA.
* Maintain and continuously improve the company’s quality management system, documentation, procedures, work instructions, and audit processes.
* Ensure compliance with customer requirements, industry standards, specifications, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Lead customer audits, supplier audits, internal audits, and customer quality reviews.
* Build strong working relationships with customer quality and engineering teams.
* Develop meaningful quality metrics, including first pass yield, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality, customer complaints, corrective action effectiveness, and supplier performance.
* Improve material traceability and process control throughout the manufacturing operation.
* Lead supplier quality development and ensure purchased materials and outside processes meet Ferry Cap requirements.
* Develop, coach, and hold accountable the quality team while strengthening quality knowledge throughout the organization.
* Support new product introduction, process changes, capital projects, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish clear containment, escalation, and corrective action processes when quality concerns arise.

**Required Qualifications**

* Significant quality leadership experience in a metal manufacturing environment.
* Strong practical knowledge of metallurgy, material properties, metal transformation, and heat treatment.
* Experience with manufacturing processes such as cold forming, forging, machining, threading, rolling, or similar metalworking operations.
* Demonstrated ability to diagnose metallurgical and manufacturing process failures.
* Experience leading quality systems, customer audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
* Strong working knowledge of dimensional inspection, mechanical testing, metallurgical testing, calibration, and measurement systems.
* Experience using quality tools such as PFMEA, control plans, SPC, MSA, 8D, and root cause analysis.
* Proven ability to work collaboratively with operations and engineering teams.
* Strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem solving skills.
* Willingness to spend significant time on the manufacturing floor and become personally involved in resolving issues.
* Bachelor’s degree in metallurgy, materials science, engineering, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant manufacturing experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive quality experience, including at least five years in a leadership role.
* Experience with engineered fasteners, high strength components, critical industrial products, or power generation applications.
* Experience with ISO based quality management systems and customer specific quality requirements.
* Experience working with commercial heat treat suppliers and internal heat treatment operations.
* ASQ certification, Six Sigma certification, or formal Lean manufacturing training.
* Experience working in a union manufacturing environment.

**Leadership Profile**

The successful candidate will be:

* Hands on and comfortable working directly with production employees.
* Collaborative and capable of building trust across departments.
* Technically strong, practical, and decisive.
* Focused on preventing defects instead of relying on inspection to find them.
* Comfortable challenging existing practices while respecting Ferry Cap’s people and history.
* Able to balance customer requirements with operational realities.
* Committed to accountability, continuous improvement, and developing others.

**Why Join Ferry Cap**

This position offers the opportunity to play a major role in the continued transformation and growth of a historic American manufacturing company. The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will have direct access to company leadership, meaningful influence over operations, and the opportunity to build a quality culture that supports Ferry Cap’s customers, employees, and long term success.

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.**  
  
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

The role offers the opportunity to influence the quality standard for a growing federal business and help prepare the organization to support additional federal programs over time.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.
* Oversee quality processes supporting receiving, quarantine, release, disposition, returns, destruction, recalls, deviations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, training, complaints and document control.
* Guide quality decisions for controlled-temperature pharmaceutical products, including refrigerated, frozen and ultra-cold storage and distribution.
* Partner with site Operations leaders and Cart.com’s Compliance team to implement operational changes required to meet quality standards and client expectations.
* Use quality metrics, audit findings, client feedback and site observations to identify risk, prioritize improvements and report progress to senior leadership.
* Travel to sites for audit preparation, team development, quality reviews and issue resolution.

**Who You Are:**

  

* You are a strategic, hands-on quality leader who can set direction while stepping into audits, excursions and site-readiness work when needed.
* You lead through others, delegate clearly, establish checkpoints and hold site quality leaders accountable for follow-through.
* You put the client’s requirements first, ask the right questions and respond with accurate, timely information.
* You communicate with credibility and composure across clients, regulators, Operations, Compliance and senior leadership.
* You are highly organized and disciplined, ensuring commitments, documentation and escalations do not get lost.
* You build strong cross-functional partnerships and can influence operational changes without creating a separate quality silo.
* You adapt to changing federal-client requirements while maintaining consistent quality standards and sound judgment.
* You develop people, address performance gaps directly and create a culture of ownership across a distributed team.

**What You’ve Done:**

  

* 7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical quality experience, including work in a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) facility and meaningful pharmaceutical distribution, logistics or 3PL quality exposure.
* 5+ years of people-leadership experience with demonstrated success delegating, developing leaders and holding teams accountable.
* Worked in pharmaceutical distribution, wholesale, logistics or third-party logistics (3PL). Manufacturing experience alone is not sufficient without meaningful distribution-quality exposure.
* Applied cGMP, Good Distribution Practice (GDP), controlled-document and standard operating procedure requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Prepared for or led audits involving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or comparable regulators, including managing responses and follow-up actions.
* Supported pharmaceutical product release, disposition, holds, recalls or temperature-excursion decisions in a regulated distribution setting.
* Written, revised or implemented quality procedures and documentation, then ensured consistent execution across teams or sites.
* Led a distributed or multi-site team and built accountability through site leaders rather than personally owning every task.
* Managed a significant client, product-quality or regulatory issue requiring coordination across Quality, Operations and Compliance.
* Earned a bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biology, chemistry or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Nice to Haves:**

  

* Background supporting federal health programs or agencies such as HHS, DLA, ASPR, BARDA, DoD or VA.
* Experience with pharmaceutical 3PLs, wholesalers, state licensing or NABP accreditation.
* Hands-on experience with vaccines or other cold-chain and ultra-cold pharmaceutical products.
* Knowledge of Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements and suspect or illegitimate product processes.
* Relevant certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Pharmaceutical GMP Professional or Lead Auditor.
* Master’s degree in a life-sciences or related discipline.
Direct leadership of quality teams  

  
  

**Physical Demands & Working Conditions:**

  

* Remote work environment with regular computer and video-conference use.
* Ability to travel by air or ground up to 30% and work onsite in warehouse, pharmaceutical distribution and temperature-controlled environments.
* Ability to move through operating areas and wear required personal protective equipment when visiting sites.

Your scope will be company-wide and your team will implement systems and processes that ensure products are designed, manufactured and shipped to the highest levels of performance, reliability, and quality.

This role is for an executive leader with experience developing new technologies and bringing high-volume manufacturing facilities to life. You will provide vision, strategy and leadership to help Form achieve manufacturing scale, cost-reduction, and daily operation execution.

Are you a quality leader who enjoys building systems, developing teams, and creating a culture of continuous improvement? Advantic Building Group is seeking a Director of Quality to lead enterprise-wide quality strategy, establish a scalable Quality Management System (QMS), drive ISO 9001 certification efforts, and partner with leaders across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and field operations to deliver exceptional customer outcomes. This is a unique opportunity to build and shape the future of quality within a growing organization.

At Advantic Building Group, we design, fabricate, and install innovative Fiber Reinforced Polymer (FRP) structural systems that help our customers build smarter, safer, and more efficiently.

But what truly sets Advantic apart isn’t just what we build — it’s **how** we work and **who** we work with.

We're a team that values ownership, camaraderie, and curiosity. We roll up our sleeves, tackle challenges together, and support one another along the way. As we continue to grow, we're looking for a quality leader who shares those values and can help strengthen the culture we've built while establishing the systems, processes, and accountability necessary to deliver exceptional quality outcomes for our customers.

**Why Join Advantic?**

* Lead the development of a scalable enterprise-wide Quality Management System (QMS)
* Drive Advantic's ISO 9001 certification journey
* Influence quality across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and field operations
* Build and develop a growing quality organization
* Partner directly with senior leadership to shape strategic initiatives
* Make a visible impact on customer success, operational excellence, and company growth

  

**Role Summary**

The Director of Quality provides strategic leadership for quality across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, assembly, and field operations. This role is responsible for developing and executing Advantic Building Group's quality strategy, building a scalable Quality Management System (QMS), leading ISO 9001 certification efforts, and driving continuous improvement throughout the organization.

This leader partners closely with operations, engineering, supply chain, and project teams to reduce defects, improve process performance, strengthen customer confidence, and support the company's growth objectives.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Quality Leadership and Strategic Planning**

* Develop and execute a quality roadmap aligned with business growth, customer commitments, operational risks, and manufacturing and construction requirements; set annual objectives, priorities, and resource needs, including staffing, inspection equipment, and quality technology.
* Report quality performance, emerging risks, and cost of poor quality (scrap, rework, field repairs, returns, warranty) to senior leadership with clear owners, deadlines, and escalation expectations, and partner with Operations and Delivery to reduce it.

**Quality Management Systems (QMS) & ISO 9001 Leadership**

* Develop, implement, and continuously improve Advantic's Quality Management System (QMS), while leading ISO 9001 certification readiness, certification audits, surveillance audits, and recertification activities.
* Build a scalable, practical Quality Management System that enables operational consistency, supports growth, improves customer satisfaction, and achieves ISO 9001 certification.
* Govern document, configuration, and revision control across engineering drawings, submittals, production information, and field documentation, and ensure quality records are reliable and accessible across ERP, MES, and document systems with defined data ownership.

**Manufacturing Quality, Process Control & Continuous Improvement**

* Establish inspection and test plans, acceptance criteria, and release controls for incoming materials, in-process fabrication, final assembly, packaging, and pre-shipment verification, ensuring products conform to approved drawings, engineering requirements, customer specifications, and applicable contractual and industry requirements.
* Partner with Operations on specification review, design reviews, process risk assessments, first-build validation, and readiness for new or changed products and processes; coordinate qualified technical resources when specialized expertise is needed.
* Define traceability, inspection records, measuring equipment controls, calibration, and measurement method validation appropriate to risk and application.
* Establish controls for FRP materials and structural assemblies, including storage, handling, fabrication, and special processes.

**Corrective Actions, Root Cause Analysis & Quality Improvement**

* Lead the enterprise nonconformance and corrective action process, including containment, material disposition, root cause analysis, escalation management, and verification of corrective action effectiveness across internal, supplier, customer, and field-related issues.
* Exercise authority under approved procedures to quarantine material, hold shipments, or stop affected work when conformity is in question; coordinate technical dispositions and obtain required customer approval for concessions or deviations, while maintaining independence of quality decisions.

**Supplier, Subcontractor, & Field Quality Management**

* Partner with Supply Chain to establish supplier qualification, approval, audit, and performance monitoring, including quality requirements for outsourced services and subcontracted work, and maintain approval status in the approved supplier system.
* Ensure certifications, traceability, inspection evidence, and customer requirements are flowed down to suppliers and verified.
* Lead supplier corrective actions and improvement plans, and support cost recovery within established commercial authority.
* Develop the field quality program for construction management and data center white space work, including project quality plan templates, inspection and test plan requirements, hold and witness points, and documentation standards that on-site QC managers must follow.
* Set expectations for, train, and hold on-site QC managers accountable to the program through project kickoffs, periodic field audits, and review of inspection records, field non-conformances, and punch list and turnover documentation.
* Serve as the escalation point for field quality issues and the senior quality contact for customers and third-party inspectors during audits and handover.

  

**Performance Measures**

* Establish baselines, targets, and reporting definitions with leadership. Measures include first-pass yield, scrap and rework, cost of poor quality, nonconformance recurrence and closure time, corrective action effectiveness, supplier performance, customer complaints, field deficiencies, audit completion, calibration compliance, and progress against the quality roadmap.

  

**People Leadership and Shared Accountability**

* Lead hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, and development of quality personnel, with training matrices, competency expectations, and succession plans.
* Partner with operational leaders to build quality awareness across the organization, and hold process owners accountable through agreed governance and escalation, reinforcing that each department owns the quality of its work.
* Model Ownership, Camaraderie, and Curiosity through clear expectations, respectful challenge, and consistent follow-through.

  

**What We're Looking For**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, quality, or a related discipline, or equivalent directly relevant experience.
* Ten or more years of progressive quality experience, including five or more years leading a quality team or function in manufacturing or a comparable technical environment.
* Demonstrated success building, implementing, or significantly improving Quality Management Systems (QMS).
* Experience leading ISO 9001 implementation, certification readiness, and managing internal, customer, and third-party audits.
* Proven results developing people, leading change across departments, and reducing defects, repeat failures, or quality-related costs.
* Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and inspection requirements; practical knowledge of measurement systems, traceability, process controls, and structured problem-solving.
* Experience using ERP, MES, electronic quality systems, or comparable tools to establish dependable workflows and actionable reporting.
* Ability to communicate clearly with customers, frontline employees, and senior leaders; make sound decisions under pressure; and resolve competing quality, schedule, and business priorities.

  

*Preferred Qualifications*

* Experience with FRP or composite products, structural fabrication, engineered assemblies, construction quality, or mission-critical and data center projects.
* Experience connecting manufacturing quality with field installation, subcontractor oversight, customer acceptance, and project turnover.
* ASQ CMQ/OE, CQE, or CQA certification; ISO 9001 lead auditor qualification; or Lean Six Sigma training with demonstrated application.

  

**Physical demands**

While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to communicate effectively through speaking and listening. The role typically involves prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer. The employee may occasionally be required to stand, walk, reach with hands and arms, and lift or move objects up to 15 pounds.

*Advantic Building Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.*

About Us

  

Skydweller Aero Inc. is a transatlantic, cutting-edge aerospace company developing solar-powered aircraft solutions capable of perpetual flight while carrying heavy and powerful payloads. Building on technology from the longest continuous renewably powered flight program in history, this fast-growing company is creating a new class of unmanned aircraft. It combines the persistence of geosynchronous satellites with the sensing capabilities and flexibility of a large airborne platform. Skydweller Aero Inc. has its global and US headquarters in Oklahoma City, with European operations headquartered in Spain.

Role Summary

  

As Skydweller prepares to move from development toward aircraft production, we are looking for an experienced manufacturing executive to build and lead our production organization. This role is based in **Oklahoma City, OK** and reports to the Chief Operating Officer.

The Vice President, Manufacturing & Production will own all aircraft production operations: final assembly, systems integration, avionics installation, production testing, factory operations and aircraft delivery. You will lead the organization as we scale from prototype and low-rate initial production into sustained manufacturing.

We are looking for a hands-on aerospace manufacturing leader with a proven track record of building production organizations, improving factory performance and delivering complex aircraft in FAA-regulated environments.

**Why join:** Most manufacturing leadership roles optimize an existing production system. This one builds it. You will establish the manufacturing organization, develop the factory workforce, and scale production of one of the most ambitious autonomous aircraft programs in aerospace.

Responsibilities

  

**Production leadership**

  

* Lead all aircraft production and manufacturing operations.
* Drive safe, efficient and repeatable aircraft production.
* Build and lead a high-performing manufacturing organization, with clear management systems, metrics and operating rhythms.
* Foster a culture of accountability, safety, quality and continuous improvement.

  

**Assembly and integration**

* Oversee final assembly, systems and electrical integration, avionics installation and aircraft completion.
* Ensure aircraft are built to engineering, quality and regulatory requirements.
* Drive production readiness and resolve manufacturing constraints and bottlenecks.

  

**Production planning and execution**

* Own execution of the Master Production Schedule.
* Lead production planning, labor allocation and resource management.
* Set capacity plans that support production-rate growth.
* Monitor factory performance and drive throughput, productivity and efficiency improvements.

  

**Production testing and acceptance**

* Lead production acceptance testing and ground test operations.
* Coordinate production readiness with Engineering, Quality, Flight Operations and Program Management.
* Ensure aircraft move smoothly from production through acceptance and delivery.

  

**Regulatory compliance and quality**

* Ensure compliance with FAA Part 21 production requirements and the company quality management system.
* Maintain production configuration control and manufacturing documentation discipline.
* Support internal, regulatory and customer audits and certification activities.
* Partner with Quality leadership to improve first-pass yield.

  

**Growth and scale-up**

* Develop the manufacturing infrastructure, facilities and staffing plans needed for higher production rates.
* Implement lean manufacturing and operational excellence initiatives.

  

**People leadership**

* Recruit, develop and mentor production leaders and technical staff.
* Establish workforce development and skills-training programs.

We’re a technology company supplying raw metal to frontier American manufacturers. We use software and automation to supply metal to factories faster than the industry thought possible.

### **The role**

We’re hiring a VP of Production to lead manufacturing performance across Nox Metals’ facilities. You will own how work moves through our factories: production planning, daily execution, capacity, staffing, quality, productivity, and on-time delivery.

This is a hands-on manufacturing leadership role with real time on the factory floor. You will develop production leaders, resolve constraints, and create repeatable ways of working that help teams deliver as demand grows. Success means safe, reliable production and clear accountability from the daily schedule through completed customer orders.

### **You will**

* Lead production execution across facilities, with clear expectations for safety, quality, output, cost, and delivery.
* Translate demand into practical production, staffing, shift, and capacity plans.
* Develop plant and production leaders who take ownership of results and build strong teams.
* Establish daily operating reviews, shift handoffs, escalation paths, and performance measures that drive action.
* Identify bottlenecks, reduce downtime and rework, and improve material flow and labor productivity.
* Build consistent training, work instructions, and qualification standards while staying close to how work happens.
* Protect material traceability and quality throughout production.
* Partner with maintenance and engineering on equipment reliability, capacity improvements, and automation.
* Work with supply chain and commercial teams to align material availability, production commitments, and customer needs.
* Partner with finance on production economics and equipment investment decisions.
* Help new or expanded facilities establish reliable production and sustain performance as they ramp.

### **You are**

* A manufacturing leader with a record of improving factory performance and developing accountable leaders.
* Experienced managing production teams, schedules, equipment constraints, and competing priorities.
* Uncompromising about safety, quality, and traceability.
* Fluent in capacity, throughput, labor productivity, downtime, and delivery performance.
* Comfortable making decisions on the floor and following through until problems are resolved.

Experience leading multiple facilities, scaling production through rapid growth, or working in metals, machining, aerospace, industrial distribution, or related environments.

Expect regular time at our manufacturing facilities and travel between sites as needed.

Nox Metals is an equal opportunity employer. We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, and the California Fair Chance Act.

**Position Overview**
---------------------

As the Director of Manufacturing, you will serve as the senior plant leader for a high-volume beverage canning operation responsible for batching, filling, seaming, and packaging canned CELSIUS® beverages. You will provide strategic and operational leadership across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, safety, warehousing, workforce development, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who has operated in a high-speed, automated food, beverage, packaging, or consumer products environment. This role requires strong business judgment, operational discipline, technical understanding, and the ability to build an accountable, collaborative culture focused on safety, food safety, quality, service, cost, and continuous improvement.

**On-Site:** Based full-time in Charlotte, NC at Big Beverages manufacturing facility

**Travel Requirements:** Up to 25% domestic travel

**People Management Responsibilities:** Yes

**Reports To:** VP of Manufacturing

**Role Type:** Full-Time

 **Requirements**  

* **Experience:** 7-10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, preferably in high-speed beverage filling/canning, food, or consumer packaged goods operations, including at least 3–5 years leading a plant or multi-department operation with full responsibility for production performance and hourly teams.
* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Food Science, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
* Experience leading high-volume, automated manufacturing operations and managing production, maintenance, engineering, quality, safety, and continuous improvement functions.
* Working knowledge of FSSC 22000, ISO 22000 principles, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, food defense, food fraud prevention, traceability, prerequisite programs, CAPA systems, and audit readiness.
* Demonstrated success improving OEE, schedule attainment, throughput, labor efficiency, yield, waste, downtime, quality, cost performance, and equipment reliability through disciplined operating systems.
* Experience managing budgets, labor planning, capital projects, business cases, and plant-level financial performance.
* Experience hiring, developing, coaching, and leading large hourly and salaried teams, including supervisors and frontline leaders.
* Experience using ERP/MRP, MES, maintenance-management, and manufacturing-performance systems to make data-driven decisions.
* Strong analytical, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to work onsite at the manufacturing facility and support a flexible schedule based on operational needs.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Master’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Food Science, or a related field.
* PCQI, HACCP, FSSC 22000, Lean Six Sigma, or similar certification or training.
* Hands-on experience with high-speed carbonated beverage filling and canning lines, including syrup batching/blending, water treatment, carbonation, fillers, can seamers and double-seam integrity, can warmers/pasteurizers, CIP sanitation, and end-of-line packaging and palletizing.
* Experience with plant start-ups, expansions, new line installations, automation, commissioning, scale-up, or major capital investments.
* Experience supporting a rapidly growing consumer brand or publicly traded company.
* Experience working with labor relations or represented manufacturing environments.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all manufacturing operations to ensure the safe, efficient, and consistent production of high-quality canned beverages from production scheduling through finished-goods handoff.
* Develop and execute the plant operating strategy in alignment with CELSIUS business objectives, demand forecasts, customer requirements, and long-term growth plans.
* Own production planning, capacity, staffing, schedule attainment, changeovers, line utilization, labor efficiency, and daily operating execution.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, warehouse, and support functions.
* Drive key operating metrics, including safety, OEE, throughput, yield, scrap, waste, downtime, labor productivity, cost per unit, on-time production, and schedule attainment.
* Establish and sustain leader standard work, tiered accountability, visual management, root-cause problem solving, standard work, and continuous-improvement routines.
* Partner with Maintenance and Engineering on preventive and predictive maintenance, equipment reliability, automation, capital priorities, commissioning, line expansions, and new technology implementation.
* Coordinate with Warehousing, Logistics, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Customer Service to maintain material availability, protect product integrity, and ensure accurate and timely finished-goods handoff.
* Maintain compliance with applicable safety, environmental, food-contact, quality, food-safety, and regulatory requirements, including FSSC 22000, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, and customer standards.
* Ensure effective prerequisite programs, food defense, food fraud prevention, sanitation, traceability, lot control, allergen control where applicable, and environmental monitoring activities.
* Oversee inspections, testing, product release, holds, deviations, nonconforming product, complaints, CAPAs, and corrective-action effectiveness in partnership with Quality.
* Ensure beverage-specific quality controls are effective, including ingredient and batch accuracy, Brix and carbonation targets, fill levels and net contents, double-seam inspection, date/lot coding, and finished-product testing.
* Lead audit readiness and support certification, surveillance, recertification, customer, regulatory, internal, and third-party audits.
* Maintain a strong safety culture through employee engagement, training, audits, risk assessments, safety observations, incident investigations, emergency preparedness, and corrective-action plans.
* Collaborate with Human Resources to recruit, develop, retain, and engage a high-performing plant workforce.
* Build leadership capability through coaching, performance management, individual development plans, skills matrices, cross-training, succession planning, and consistent leader standard work.
* Lead labor planning and workforce optimization in response to production volumes, seasonality, new product requirements, and business growth.
* Manage the plant operating budget, labor costs, maintenance spending, capital expenditures, and other controllable expenses.
* Analyze operational and financial data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and actions needed to improve plant performance.
* Communicate plant performance, operating priorities, business risks, resource needs, and improvement plans clearly to plant and executive leadership.
* Contribute to network and growth planning, including capacity, new product introductions, and line additions, in partnership with corporate Operations and Supply Chain.
* Build strong working relationships with corporate brand, R&D/innovation, Quality, and Supply Chain partners, as well as co-pack customers and key suppliers where applicable.
* Promote a culture consistent with CELSIUS values, including ownership, agility, grit, commercial thinking, collaboration, positive influence, and a bias for action.
* Provide site-wide leadership that translates company goals into plant priorities, targets, and daily execution.
* Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.
* Leadership Expectations
* Lead with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.

* Maintain high standards for safety, food safety, quality, compliance, and operational execution.

### **Physical Demands and Work Environment**

This role is based on the manufacturing floor and in plant offices. The work environment includes high-speed automated equipment, elevated noise levels requiring hearing protection, wet floors, temperature variation, and forklift traffic. Required PPE (such as safety glasses, hearing protection, and safety footwear) must be worn in production areas, and all plant safety, GMP, and food-safety rules must be followed. The role regularly requires standing and walking for extended periods and climbing stairs and platforms, and occasionally lifting up to 25 pounds. This position may be eligible for other compensation, including bonuses and Restricted Stock Units (subject to company plans).*

**DEFINITION:**

Under general direction from the General Manager, plans, directs, organizes, integrates and provides oversight of ReGen Monterey’s Materials Recovery Facility (MRF), equipment maintenance, site and facilities maintenance, landfill operations; scales operations, landfill gas operations, and Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) operations; directs and manages the development of short and long-term goals and objectives consistent with the Strategic Plan and annual business plan and ensures their effective execution; ensures all assigned operations and functions serve the needs of ReGen Monterey, while complying with applicable laws and regulations; responsible for maximizing the environmental management of resources; provides highly responsible and complex operations support to the General Manager.

**DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS:**

This position is responsible for coordination, integration and short and long-range planning of a wide variety of functions related to solid waste processing, recycling and diversion programs for ReGen Monterey. Incumbents work at an advanced professional level on complex and specialized solid waste-related operations, recycling activities, facilities, programs, and services, which include formulation and implementation of programs and financial budgets. Within assigned areas of accountability, the incumbent operates with substantial latitude and discretion to achieve effective and efficient utilization of resources in serving ReGen Monterey’s mission. Positions at this class level serve as a member of ReGen’s leadership team and provide advice and counsel to the General Manager regarding strategic policy and problem-solving issues relating to the assigned Departments and ReGen’s overall. A person appointed to the Director of Operations classification is an “at-will” employee.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

*The following duties are typical of this classification and are intended only to describe the various types of work that may be performed, the level of technical complexity of the assignment(s) and are not intended to be an all-inclusive list of duties. The omission of a specific duty statement does not exclude it from the position if the work is consistent with the concept of the classification or is similar or closely related to another duty statement to address business needs and changing business practices.*

* Oversee and is responsible for planning and execution of all aspects of solid waste and recycling operations including processing, recycling/diversion, scheduling, expansion and renovation of processing facility, and customer service.
* Oversee logistics, material preparation and export compliance of collected materials and manage all aspects of commodity sales and related contracted services.
* Oversees and is responsible for the planning and execution of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of ReGen Monterey’s landfill; oversees proper compliance with specifications on the use and development of disposal site, ensures proper operations compliance with health and safety regulations.
* Participates in the development and implementation of goals, objectives, policies, and priorities of ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Plans, organizes, controls, integrates and evaluates the work of assigned departments to ensure services comply with the policies and strategic direction set by the General Manager, Board of Directors and all applicable laws and regulations.
* Recommend and enforce State waste reduction/recycling regulations and other policy issues, including safety policy and procedures.
* Manages the development, revision, and implementation of policies and procedures for ReGen Monterey’s solid waste and recycling/diversion operations.
* Drafts budget for assigned departments.
* Reviews and assesses all program production data; measures program effectiveness; prepares quarterly and annual data reports.
* Assists in the preparation of Requests for Proposal (RFPs) for equipment and services; represents the division in negotiations with vendors and service contractors and participates in contract administration in disputed contractual matters.
* Prepares staff reports and letters, including reports for presentation to Board of Directors.
* All ReGen Monterey positions require the employee to provide good customer service to both internal and external customers, maintain positive and effective working relationships with other ReGen Monterey employees, and have regular and reliable attendance and timeliness. Must show cooperation and respect to fellow employees and supervisors at all times.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBLITIES:**

The incumbent in this position provides direct supervision of the operations department managers and has oversight of multiple departments and indirect supervision of approximately 100 assigned department employees.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Through subordinates, supervises the safe and efficient handling and disposal of solid waste, including household, industrial, infectious, medical, and household hazardous materials; provides oversight ancillary solid waste operations, including equipment maintenance and repair, recycling, and enforcement of refuse disposal laws.
* Coordinates solid waste processing operations with engineering staff to ensure the success of new programs and facilities; analyzes field operations and formulates improvements to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations; performs long-range planning for staffing needs, equipment replacement, and other operational requirements.
* Provides oversight to HHW program and organics recycling program, including food waste collection, yard waste processing, mulch/compost marketing and other waste reduction processing such as scrap metal, electronic waste, mattresses, and scrap tires.

* Prepares tonnage reports and makes recommendations regarding change in fees.
* Organize and optimize the structure of the assigned departments, adjusting in accordance with workloads and new/changing functions.
* Maintain contact with various governmental and regulatory agencies, industry related agencies, and represent ReGen Monterey at public and professional organizations functions.
* Selects and trains operations staff; assists management staff in resolving the most difficult operational problems; establishes productive standards and measures staff performance; accordingly, prepares annual performance plans, evaluates performance, and reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinate managers. Collaborates with human resources with disciplinary actions.
* Directly or through subordinates, responds to complaints from ReGen Monterey customers by explaining and enforcing applicable laws and regulations; participates in public workshops to explain and generate support for proposed projects and facilities; may address the Board of Directors to answer questions about issues or proposals related to ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Oversees and participates in the annual review and revision of ReGen Monterey’s fee structure; develops strategies and approaches for evaluating fee change alternatives; directs the development and recommends proposed fees; attends and participates in public meetings; oversees the implementation of new fees following board approval.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Strategic Execution

* Support facility expansions, production transitions, new product introductions, and other strategic manufacturing initiatives.
* Translate company objectives into actionable manufacturing plans with measurable results.

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including at least 5 years in a senior management or director-level role.
* Demonstrated experience overseeing large-scale manufacturing operations with multiple departments, production teams, and supervisory personnel.
* Proven success improving production output, operational efficiency, labor productivity, and manufacturing performance.

**Preferred Qualifications**

**Compensation Range:**

$122,800 - $204,600

**Plant Manager**

Department: Operations / Manufacturing

Reports To: Director of Operations

Direct Reports: Production Managers, Facilities Manager, and other assigned manufacturing leadership

Scope: Three manufacturing buildings / multi-product HVAC manufacturing operation

**Position**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, performance, and day-to-day execution of manufacturing operations across three buildings within a large HVAC manufacturing facility. This position provides hands-on leadership to ensure the plant safely produces high-quality products on schedule, at the required volume and cost, while developing a strong culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

The Plant Manager is responsible for coordinating production activities across multiple manufacturing processes and buildings, including assembly, sheet metal fabrication, welding, piping/refrigeration, testing, material flow, and final product completion.

The successful candidate will establish clear operating standards, drive cross-functional accountability, develop manufacturing leadership, remove operational constraints, and ensure the plant has the people, processes, equipment, and infrastructure required to support current production and future growth.

This position is expected to be highly visible on the manufacturing floor and serves as the primary operational leader responsible for translating business objectives into daily execution.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Plant Leadership & Operational Execution**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for manufacturing operations across all three buildings.
* Establish daily, weekly, and monthly operating priorities aligned with business requirements.
* Ensure production plans are executed safely, efficiently, and according to customer commitments.
* Maintain strong communication and coordination between buildings and manufacturing departments.
* Establish clear ownership and accountability for production performance.
* Lead daily plant operating reviews and ensure corrective actions are completed.
* Identify and remove constraints affecting throughput, capacity, quality, or delivery.
* Maintain appropriate production capacity, staffing, equipment, and infrastructure to support business growth.
* Ensure standardized processes are consistently followed across all buildings.
* Maintain a strong management presence on the manufacturing floor.

**2. Production Management**

* Lead Production Managers and ensure effective management of production personnel.
* Establish production priorities based on customer demand, capacity, material availability, and schedule requirements.
* Ensure production schedules are achieved while balancing labor, equipment, materials, and testing capacity.
* Monitor production flow from fabrication through final assembly and testing.
* Develop and maintain effective production metrics and visual management systems.
* Identify bottlenecks and implement corrective actions to improve throughput.
* Ensure appropriate escalation processes are in place when production performance is at risk.
* Coordinate production activities between the three buildings to maximize overall plant capacity.

**3. Safety, Environmental & Compliance**

* Establish safety as the facility’s highest operational priority.
* Partner with EHS leadership to maintain a strong safety culture across all three buildings.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental regulations, company requirements, and applicable industry standards.
* Drive accountability for safe work practices at all levels of the organization.
* Ensure timely investigation and corrective action following incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions.
* Support programs designed to reduce injuries, ergonomic risks, environmental impacts, and workplace hazards.
* Ensure employees receive appropriate safety training and understand their responsibilities.

**4. Quality**

* Partner with Quality leadership to ensure products meet customer, engineering, and company requirements.
* Establish accountability for first-time quality and defect prevention.
* Drive reduction of scrap, rework, warranty issues, and production defects.
* Ensure quality issues are rapidly escalated and contained.
* Support root-cause analysis and corrective-action processes.
* Promote quality at the source rather than relying on downstream inspection.
* Maintain compliance with the plant's quality management system and ISO requirements.

**5. Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead the implementation and sustainability of Lean Manufacturing Principles throughout all three buildings.
* Establish a culture of continuous improvement and employee involvement.
* Drive 5S, visual management, standardized work, problem solving, waste elimination, and flow improvements.
* Support Value Stream Mapping and improvement of end-to-end product flow.
* Establish measurable improvement targets for productivity, quality, delivery, inventory, and cost.
* Partner with Lean/Manufacturing Engineering leadership to prioritize improvement projects based on business impact.
* Ensure Lean improvements are sustained through management systems and standard work.
* Develop frontline leaders capable of independently identifying and solving operational problems.

**6. People Leadership & Organizational Development**

* Develop a high-performing manufacturing leadership team.
* Establish clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
* Coach and develop Production Managers, Supervisors, and other manufacturing leaders.
* Identify organizational capability gaps and work with Human Resources to develop staffing and development plans.
* Support workforce planning and hiring activities necessary to meet production requirements.
* Establish effective onboarding and training processes for new employees.
* Develop succession plans for key manufacturing positions.
* Promote employee engagement, teamwork, ownership, and accountability.
* Address performance issues promptly and consistently.

**7. Capacity & Business Growth**

* Develop manufacturing capacity plans to support current and future customer demand.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Finance, Materials, and other functions to identify capacity requirements.
* Evaluate labor, equipment, floor space, testing, utilities, and infrastructure requirements.
* Support capital planning and justification for new equipment and facility improvements.
* Ensure new production areas and buildings are effectively integrated into the overall manufacturing system.
* Develop ramp-up plans for new products, programs, and production transfers.
* Ensure the plant can scale production without compromising safety, quality, or delivery performance.

**8. Cross-Functional Leadership**

Work closely with:

* Director of Operations
* Production
* Materials
* Production Planning
* Logistics
* Quality
* EHS
* Lean / Manufacturing Engineering
* Facilities
* Maintenance
* Engineering
* Finance
* Human Resources
* Supply Chain
* Sales / Customer teams

Ensure cross-functional issues are identified early, assigned to the appropriate owner, and driven to resolution.

**9. Facilities, Equipment & Infrastructure**

* Partner with Facilities and Maintenance leadership to ensure buildings, utilities, production equipment, cranes, test infrastructure, and other critical assets support production requirements.
* Establish preventive and predictive maintenance expectations.
* Ensure critical production equipment has appropriate contingency plans.
* Support capital equipment selection, installation, commissioning, and production launch.
* Ensure facility expansion projects are integrated into manufacturing operations with minimal disruption to production.

**10. Performance Management & Accountability**

Establish and maintain a plant operating system based on measurable performance.

Key performance indicators should include:

Safety

* Recordable incident rate
* Lost-time incidents
* Near misses
* Safety observations
* Corrective-action closure

Quality

* First-pass yield
* Scrap
* Rework
* Customer defects
* Warranty / quality escapes

Delivery

* On-time delivery
* Schedule attainment
* Production attainment
* Manufacturing lead time
* Test-bay utilization / throughput

Productivity

* Labor productivity
* Units per labor hour
* OEE where applicable
* Direct labor efficiency
* Throughput

Cost

* Manufacturing cost
* Labor variance
* Scrap cost
* Overtime
* Cost of poor quality

Lean

* 5S performance
* Kaizen completion
* Standard work compliance
* Improvement savings
* Value-stream performance

The Plant Manager will ensure performance is reviewed routinely and that corrective actions have clearly identified owners and due dates.

**Leadership Expectations**

The Plant Manager is expected to:

* Lead from the floor rather than from the office.
* Establish a culture of accountability without creating a culture of blame.
* Make decisions based on facts and data.
* Escalate issues early rather than allowing problems to become emergencies.
* Develop leaders instead of personally solving every problem.
* Maintain a strong focus on safety and quality while driving production.
* Create alignment between the three buildings rather than allowing them to operate as independent plants.
* Establish consistent standards and expectations across the operation.
* Communicate clearly with employees, leadership, and cross-functional partners.
* Demonstrate urgency while maintaining disciplined problem solving.
* Build an organization capable of supporting significant business growth.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field preferred.
* 7+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 3+ years of plant or multi-department manufacturing management experience.
* Experience managing large manufacturing organizations, multiple production areas, and facilities.
* Experience in HVAC, refrigeration, industrial equipment, sheet metal, welding, assembly, or related manufacturing strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience managing significant production growth or plant expansion.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Demonstrated experience managing safety, quality, delivery, and cost performance.
* Strong financial and business acumen.
* Experience developing and leading supervisors and managers.
* Strong communication and organizational skills.
* Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth manufacturing environment.

CAMS is looking for a Plant Manager at the Kings Mountain Energy Center in Kings Mountain, NC. The incumbent will have 19 direct and indirect employees. The Plant Manager is responsible for the safe, reliable, compliant, and financially responsible operation and maintenance of the Kings Mountain Energy Center.

Kings Mountain Energy Center is a 475MW natural gas-fired combined-cycle power plant. The facility features an advanced 276MW Mitsubishi M501GAC gas turbine, a Vogt Power heat recovery steam generator (HRSG), a 225MW Toshiba steam turbine generator, and a Thermal Engineering International surface condenser.

The position provides overall leadership for plant operations, maintenance, engineering support, environmental and regulatory compliance, administration, workforce development, budgeting, outage execution, and continuous improvement. The Plant Manager serves as the primary site representative to CAMS leadership, facility ownership and asset management, and is accountable for developing a high-performing organization that maximizes plant availability, reliability, efficiency, and long-term asset value. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong leadership, sound technical and business judgment, and the ability to manage a complex combined-cycle generating facility in a competitive power-market environment.

### **Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for the safe, reliable, environmentally compliant, and cost-effective operation and maintenance of the facility.
* Establish and maintain a strong safety culture in which employees and contractors actively identify hazards, stop unsafe work, and demonstrate personal ownership of safety performance.
* Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental permits, laws, regulations, NERC requirements, OSHA requirements, company policies, and facility procedures.
* Lead and develop the plant management team and workforce, including recruiting, coaching, performance management, succession planning, qualification programs, and workforce development.
* Maintain effective working relationships with facility ownership, Asset Management, CAMS leadership, regulatory agencies, the system operator, utilities, OEMs, contractors, and other key stakeholders.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, O&M budgets, capital plans, forecasts, and long-term maintenance strategies consistent with owner objectives and contractual requirements.
* Monitor plant financial performance and control expenditures while ensuring that short-term budget objectives do not create unacceptable safety, environmental, reliability, or long-term asset risk.
* Direct plant operations to achieve availability, reliability, heat-rate, start-reliability, capacity, and other performance objectives while meeting dispatch and commercial obligations.
* Provide leadership for maintenance strategies, preventive and predictive maintenance, corrective-maintenance backlog management, equipment reliability, root-cause analysis, and elimination of recurring failures.
* Direct planning and execution of combustion turbine, steam turbine, HRSG, generator, electrical, and balance-of-plant outages and major maintenance activities, including scope, budget, schedule, contractor performance, quality, and risk management.
* Develop and maintain multi-year outage, major-maintenance, and capital improvement plans based on equipment condition, OEM recommendations, operating profile, commercial requirements, and risk.
* Identify significant plant risks and provide CAMS leadership and ownership with timely information, alternatives, consequences, and clear recommendations for decision-making.
* Ensure appropriate critical-spares strategy, inventory controls, long-lead component planning, and equipment-obsolescence management.
* Oversee plant engineering and technical support activities, including equipment modifications, controls and logic changes, performance monitoring, capital projects, and technical problem solving.
* Ensure plant procedures, drawings, technical documentation, training materials, emergency plans, and operating records are accurate and maintained.
* Oversee administration of applicable plant contracts and agreements and ensure operational compliance with owner requirements, O&M obligations, OEM/LTSA requirements, fuel and utility agreements, and other commercial commitments.
* Maintain effective communication with Asset Management and ownership, including prompt escalation of significant safety, environmental, operational, equipment, financial, contractual, or regulatory events.
* Lead emergency response and business-continuity activities and ensure the facility is prepared for severe weather, grid emergencies, fuel interruptions, cyber events, and major equipment failures.
* Promote a culture of accountability, teamwork, continuous improvement, and open communication across Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Compliance, and Administration.
* Identify and implement opportunities to improve plant performance, reduce operating risk, optimize costs, and increase long-term asset value.
* Support CAMS fleet initiatives, peer reviews, lessons learned, workforce-development efforts, and cross-facility technical support as requested.

Other duties as assigned.

### **Qualifications and Skills**

* 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in power generation operations and maintenance, including significant leadership experience in a power plant environment.
* Prior Plant Manager, Operations Manager, Maintenance Manager, or comparable senior power-generation leadership experience strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge of combined-cycle power plant operations, maintenance, reliability, and major equipment systems. Experience with combustion turbines, steam turbines, HRSGs, generators, electrical systems, and balance-of-plant equipment is preferred.
* Experience with Mitsubishi M501GAC combustion turbines is preferred.
* Demonstrated experience planning and executing major outages, managing contractors and OEMs, controlling outage scope and cost, and resolving emergent technical issues.
* Working knowledge of environmental, health and safety, and electric-generation regulatory requirements applicable to power plant operations.
* Demonstrated experience developing and managing O&M budgets, forecasts, capital projects, and long-term maintenance plans.
* Proven ability to lead, coach, develop, and hold accountable a multidisciplinary workforce.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, planning, and organizational skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with employees, executives, owners, regulators, contractors, and technical personnel.
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field preferred. Significant relevant power-generation leadership experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and familiarity with computerized maintenance management systems, plant historians, performance-monitoring systems, and other power-plant business systems.
* Ability to respond to plant emergencies and significant operating events outside normal business hours as required.

Other Desirable Skills

* Demonstrates visible leadership and a strong personal commitment to safety and environmental compliance.
* Balances technical, operational, financial, and commercial considerations when making decisions.
* Communicates significant risks and problems early and avoids surprises for ownership and senior leadership.
* Demonstrates strong customer service skills and the ability to build trusted relationships with facility ownership and Asset Management.
* Effectively prioritizes competing demands in a fast-changing operating environment.
* Develop people and create clear succession paths for key positions.
* Demonstrates a high degree of integrity, accountability, sound judgment, and ownership mentality.
* Ability to represent the facility and CAMS professionally with owners, regulators, industry organizations, and external stakeholders

Applicants must possess a **valid driver's license** and maintain a clean driving record, as this position requires occasional travel for company business. Candidates should be comfortable operating a vehicle as part of their job responsibilities and must meet any applicable company and insurance requirements.

CAMS offers a variety of excellent benefits. Full-time employees are offered the following: medical, dental, vision, LTD, STD, and Life insurance plans. You can even select additional “al la carte” benefits to meet all your needs. You can also enroll in our 401k, flex spending accounts for medical and childcare needs, and participate in our employee referral and tuition reimbursement programs.

Qualified Applicants must be legally authorized for employment in the United States. Qualified Applicants will not require employer sponsored work authorization now or in the future for employment in the United States.

We believe in transparency and providing candidates with important information to make informed decisions. The salary range for this position will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, and location. Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to skills, experience, and relevant qualifications.

This range represents the base salary and does not include other forms of compensation, such as bonuses, benefits, or equity, which may be offered in addition to the base pay. The company reserves the right to modify.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

In this role, you will guide enterprise-wide continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen operational performance, enhance quality, and increase efficiency across multiple manufacturing sites. You will lead efforts that reduce waste, improve process capability, and support teams in optimizing complex aerospace and defense production workflows, helping ensure mission-critical hardware is delivered with consistent excellence.

#### **Duties/Responsibilities**

* Develops and deploys a multi-site continuous improvement roadmap aligned with corporate objectives.
* Leads lean, six sigma, and value stream mapping initiatives to drive operational excellence.
* Identifies and eliminates non value added activities across machining, fabrication, and downstream processing.
* Develops, tracks, and reports enterprise metrics for cost savings, yield improvements, and cycle time reduction.
* Partners with manufacturing engineering, quality, and supply chain to improve process capabilities.
* Facilitates advanced root cause problem solving activities to address systemic production bottlenecks.
* Plans and executes kaizen events focused on setup reduction, 5S workplace organization, and cellular manufacturing.
* Mentors and develops employees in lean and six sigma methodologies.
* Ensures continuous improvement initiatives support and maintain AS9100 and product safety standards.

#### **Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations management, or a related technical field.
* Minimum 8-10 years of operations or continuous improvement leadership in aerospace and defense manufacturing.
* Certified lean six sigma master black belt or black belt.
* Experience with AS9100 quality management systems and defense contract management agency (DCMA) oversight.
* Background in precision machining, structural fabrication, or aerospace assemblies.
* Proficiency with enterprise resource planning (ERP) and manufacturing execution system (MES) data analysis.

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of business administration (MBA) or master's degree.

#### **Special Mentions**

* Travel is required across regional manufacturing sites.

#### **Benefits**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off
* Health savings account (HSA) with company contribution
* Flexible spending accounts (FSA)
* Company-paid life and AD&D insurance
* Short- and long-term disability coverage
* Tuition reimbursement

Karman Space and Defense is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

existing_roles.description:
**About Carrier**

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure safe transport of food, lifesaving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit corporate.carrier.com or follow on Carrier social media at @Carrier.

**About the Job**
-----------------

The Senior Manager, LCML Fulfillment Operations leads the end-to-end order fulfillment and distribution execution operating model for Carrier's Light Commercial (LCML) HVAC business within Climate Solutions Americas (CSA). Reporting to CSA Logistics & Supply Chain leadership, this role balances customer service reliability, on-time in-full (OTIF) delivery performance, inventory allocation governance, and fulfillment cost-to-serve productivity across North America.

This leader directs a team of fulfillment operations planners, order management specialists, and execution coordinators, steering initiatives in order backlog reduction, multi-site distribution throughput, order consolidation, and peak seasonal readiness. Working collaboratively with Light Commercial SIOP, Manufacturing Operations, Distribution Center (DC) Operations, Transportation, and Commercial Sales leadership, the Senior Manager establishes fulfillment KPIs and SLAs, enhances ERP/WMS/TMS data integrity, and champions continuous improvement across the order-to-delivery ecosystem.

**Work Arrangement:** Hybrid: 3 days in office at the Atlanta Digital Hub, 2 days remote per week.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* **Fulfillment Execution & Planning Governance:** Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of fulfillment planners and execution coordinators managing day-to-day order allocation, scheduling, and customer delivery execution across North American distribution networks.
* **Network Throughput & Cost-to-Serve Productivity:** Drive order consolidation programs, warehouse/fulfillment cycle-time reductions, avoidable expedite elimination, and measurable cost-to-serve efficiencies across LCML distribution hubs.
* **Order Backlog & SLA Performance Management:** Own fulfillment scorecard reviews, OTIF delivery metrics, order-to-ship cycle times, and aged backlog governance. Partner with DC Operations and Transportation to optimize fulfillment capacity and SLA compliance.
* **Exception Management & Disruption Recovery:** Lead proactive operational recovery for critical customer delivery delays, inventory allocation constraints, capacity crunches, and seasonal demand surges.
* **Cross-Functional Alignment:** Partner strategically with Light Commercial SIOP, Manufacturing Plants, Customer Service, and Commercial Sales leadership to align inventory positioning, product launch (NPI) fulfillment readiness, and customer lead-time commitments.
* **Digital Fulfillment & Systems Enhancement:** Enhance ERP, WMS, and TMS workflow standardization, end-to-end order visibility, automated milestone tracking, and digital executive KPI dashboards.
* **Continuous Improvement & Standard Work:** Implement standardized operating procedures (SOPs), daily tier accountability cadences, and root-cause problem solving (Lean, DMAIC, 5-Why) to sustain fulfillment gains and customer satisfaction.

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Operations, Industrial Engineering, or a business discipline.
* 8+ years of progressive experience in fulfillment operations, order management, distribution center operations, or domestic supply chain logistics.
* 5+ years of direct people leadership experience managing fulfillment planners, supervisors, dispatchers, or operations analysts.
* 2+ years of hands-on experience with Enterprise ERP, Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), or Transportation Management Systems (TMS) such as SAP, Oracle, Blue Yonder/JDA, or Manhattan.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, or Master of Business Administration (MBA).
* Professional supply chain or continuous improvement credentials such as APICS (CSCP, CPIM, CLTD) or Lean Six Sigma Green/Black Belt.
* Background in commercial/light commercial HVAC, industrial equipment manufacturing, or high-SKU seasonal distribution environments.
* Strong analytical aptitude with business intelligence tools (Power BI, Tableau, advanced Excel) and data-driven executive presentations.
* Willingness to travel domestically (approximately 15–25%) to regional distribution centers, manufacturing facilities, and logistics operational hubs.

**Pay Range**

The annual salary for this position is between $117,500.00 - $234,500.00 annually. Factors which may affect pay within this range include, but are not limited to, skills, education, experience, and other unique qualifications of the successful candidate.
